proposals.title: United Kingdom — Financial Services Act 2012, chapter 21, as enacted
proposals.use: Distinct consumer/integrity/competition and prudential safety/soundness objectives; no requirement to prevent every firm failure; resource efficiency, proportionality and transparency principles.
proposals.verification: Official 385-page PDF retrieved; read assent page (printed1), section6 insertion of FSMA1B–1E (printed20–22), 2B and2G (printed29/31), 3B (printed34–35), and sections121–122 (printed210). No whole-Act review claimed.
proposals.jurisdiction: United Kingdom; section 121 specifies England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
proposals.legal_status: Enacted primary legislation, deliberately used as historical text. Assent is not assumed to commence every provision; no current consolidated-law claim.
proposals.limits: Not a capital ratio, automatic resolution power, enforcement outcome or welfare optimum. Section122 leaves remaining commencement to Treasury orders, not inspected here. Later amendments and institutional changes are outside this historical snapshot.

proposals.title: Financial Stability Board — Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions, revised version2024
proposals.use: Continuity and orderly exit; bail-in loss allocation/conversion; creditor hierarchy and liquidation-comparator compensation; temporary resolution funding with explicit conditions and loss recovery; authority independence/accountability.
proposals.verification: Actual94-page PDF: foreword printed1–2; preamble4–5; KA1.1 and2.1–2.5, printed6–7; KA3.5–3.6, printed10; KA5.1–5.2, printed12; KA6.1–6.5, printed13. Publication page confirms the2024 revision concerns FMI annex guidance.
proposals.jurisdiction: International standard; domestic implementation and authority remain separate.
proposals.legal_status: FSB resolution standard with implementation guidance. The foreword distinguishes the twelve Key Attributes from their annex guidance; neither supplies a particular national statutory power.
proposals.limits: No promise that recapitalisation creates cash, every creditor is protected, public liquidity is never used, or a national authority has these powers. Annexes, CCP calibration and country implementation are not comprehensively reviewed.
